newsitem.title: USA: Caltron to merge with J-Bird Records.
newsitem.headline: Caltron to merge with J-Bird Records.

text.p: Caltron Inc said Tuesday it will end its its relationship with private Applied Advanced Technologies Inc and will merge with private J-Bird Records Inc.
Applied will pay Caltron $350,000 plus interest and swap its restricted Caltron shares for Caltron's 45 percent stake in Applied, a Caltron spokesman said.

"Applied wanted to be released from the contract with us," the spokesman said. "The president (of the company) has finally realized what his company's technology is worth and now he doesn't want to share it."
Applied developed a proprieatary electron beam used in printing processes, the spokesman added.

Caltron signed a letter of intent to merge with J-Bird Records, a company that features artists on the Internet. The spokesman declined to elaborate on the deal but said the Caltron may change its name to reflect the merger.

Finanlly, Caltron said it is selling its interest in a pending patent on a renal ozone sterilization system to a group of investors for an undisclosed price. The patent is jointly held by Caltron, inventor Brooks Porter and the Rhode Island Renal Institute in Wakefield, R.I., the spokesman said.
Shares of the technology and investment firm traded at 1-1/2 Tuesday afternoon, up 1/16 but a long way from their 52-week high of 15.
